ask: We're an agency. Acme wants to sign off every post before it goes out. Set that up and get next week's 4 drafts to them.

steps.why: Acme's row gives the brand's clock and review mode. It does not show whether client sign-off is required, so that is read from a post next.
Next week's 4 drafts, numbered with account and full text, so the user sees exactly what the client will see. A row already out with a reviewer would carry waiting_on_client names.
client_signoff.required tells whether the brand already requires sign-off; state says not_sent, waiting_on_client or signed_off. Here required is false: the switch is off.
Who is on the brand. Acme's client reviewer shows as role reviewer, so the drafts can go to them once they are invited. Missing on this app: ask by name.

say: Here's how I'd set it up for Acme. Every post must have their yes: that's the "Client sign-off required" switch in Acme's settings, Approvals section. Only your organization owner can turn it on, and it pulls any scheduled post without a client yes back to waiting, so turn it on before scheduling. Invite Acme's approver as a client reviewer in People & access (no seat). Mark someone required only if their own yes is a must. Once they're invited, I can send these 4 drafts to them on your yes; they get an email and reminders on days 2 and 5. Don't move a time after sending: the client saw it, and a new one means sending again. I'll check where each post stands whenever you ask.
never: Saying the drafts were sent to the client before a send to them succeeded.
Approving the drafts for the team to save the client a step.
Telling a creator they can approve any post for the team: a creator approves only Bolta's drafts and posts naming them reviewer, and a refusal names the role.
Moving a post's time while the client hasn't answered without saying it voids the request.
